ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening under FICA s 21 read with s 28A against the FIC Targeted Financial Sanctions list, the United Nations Security Council consolidated sanctions list, the OFAC SDN list for any USD-based exposure, the EU consolidated financial sanctions list, and the South African domestic PEP database. Enhanced due diligence is required where any director, shareholder, UBO, or authorized signatory is a PEP, has prior adverse AML findings, or is connected to a high-risk jurisdiction. Full CDD records and UBO registers must be retained for at least 5 years after termination of the business relationship.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Companies and Intellectual Property Commission (CIPC) e-Services portal: https://eservices.cipc.co.za
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Proposed company names must be submitted in Latin script. The name may be in one or more of the 11 official South African languages (English, Afrikaans, isiZulu, isiXhosa, Sesotho, Setswana, Sepedi, Sesotho sa Leboa, Xitsonga, siSwati, Tshivenda). Where the chosen name is not in English, an English translation or transliteration must be provided for CIPC assessment. Names in non-Latin scripts such as Arabic, Chinese, Cyrillic, or Devanagari must first be transliterated into Latin characters and may be refused where the transliteration is misleading, offensive, or confusingly similar.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: A name reservation may be extended prior to expiry by filing an extension application through the CIPC e-Services portal. If the name is rejected, the applicant may submit a written request for reasons, followed by an administrative review application to the CIPC through the same portal within 20 business days of rejection. If the CIPC maintains the refusal, the applicant may apply to the Companies Tribunal under section 4 of the Companies Act 71 of 2008 for an order setting aside the CIPC decision, and thereafter may seek judicial review in the High Court. A re-submission under a slightly modified name is also permitted after the initial negative clearance.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permissible for a low-risk EdTech subscription company provided the virtual office supplies a physical South African street address capable of receiving legal service and statutory correspondence during ordinary business hours. A pure digital/post-office-box-only arrangement does not satisfy section 23 of the Companies Act 71 of 2008 requiring an accessible registered office.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: For an ISIC 6201 EdTech company with no physical consumer premises and a low AML/CFT risk tier, the estimated probability of an unannounced physical inspection by CIPC, FIC, or another competent authority in the first 12 months is approximately 3%. The likelihood rises to 12–15% if a UBO filing discrepancy, adverse sanctions/PEP match, or material non-compliance with the registered office mandate occurs.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Companies Act, 2008 (Act No. 71 of 2008); ss13(1) (incorporation), s19(1) (separate legal personality), s66 (board of directors), s70 (company secretary), together with the Companies Regulations, 2011 and Form CoR 14.1 (Notice of Incorporation).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Companies and Intellectual Property Commission (CIPC), an agency of the Department of Trade, Industry and Competition, Republic of South Africa.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Notice of Incorporation (Form CoR 14.1) read together with the Memorandum of Incorporation (MOI).
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No minimum paid-up share capital is prescribed by the Companies Act 71 of 2008 for a Proprietary Limited Company; a nominal issue of at least one share is sufficient. No escrow account is required. Shares may be issued to non-residents.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED THAT: The subscribers to the Memorandum of Incorporation hereby approve the adoption and filing of the Notice of Incorporation with the Companies and Intellectual Property Commission; the incorporation of the Company as a Proprietary Limited Company is ratified; the subscribers' subscription for shares is accepted and shares allotted in accordance with the MOI; the provisional directors are appointed to hold office until the first annual general meeting; the registered office is fixed at [address]; the first directors are authorised to attend to statutory registrations, open bank accounts, appoint auditors or a registered accountant, and take all ancillary actions to commence business. Confirmed by unanimous consent.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Company Name Reservation and Availability Search
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct a name availability search on the BizPortal public search facility. File Form CoR 9.1 submitting at least four proposed company names in order of preference. Pay the prescribed name reservation fee. The reserved name is valid for six months. The name must not be identical or confusingly similar to an existing registered name and must not contravene the Companies Act or public policy.
required_dossiers: Certified copy of ID or passport of each incorporator/director
Proof of street and postal address
Power of attorney if filing through an agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected, CIPC issues a notice citing the grounds under s11 of the Companies Act. Correct by refiling with new names or, if the reservation expires, apply for an extension using Form CoR 9.5.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Preparation and Execution of Memorandum of Incorporation and Notice of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Incorporators and first directors; CIPC for subsequent filing
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the Memorandum of Incorporation using Schedule 1 default provisions as the baseline, incorporating any permitted alternative provisions such as share class rights, director authority and quorum rules. Complete Form CoR 14.1 (Notice of Incorporation). Have each incorporator sign the MOI. For a standard (Pty) Ltd, no minimum capital is required; a nominal share capital of R1 or one share is acceptable.
required_dossiers: Signed and dated Memorandum of Incorporation
Certified identity documents of all incorporators
Consent to Act as Director forms (Form CoR 14.2)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: CIPC will query signature inconsistencies, invalidity of MOI provisions, or non-payment. Correct the documents and resubmit through BizPortal within three business days; a resubmission fee may apply.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: CIPC Filing, Registration and Issuance of Incorporation Certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Companies and Intellectual Property Commission (CIPC) e-services
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the signed MOI, Form CoR 14.1, directors' consents, name reservation number and all supporting documents via the CIPC BizPortal. Pay the applicable registration fee. CIPC performs a document consistency check and, if compliant, registers the company, assigns a unique company registration number, and issues a Registration Certificate. The company acquires legal personality under s19(1)(b) of the Companies Act from the effective date on the certificate.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application is rejected or suspended, review CIPC's non-compliance statement, cure the identified defects, upload corrected forms in the same application, and request re-instatement. If the name is objectionable, substitute an approved alternative name.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Convene First Board Meeting and Adopt Authorising Resolutions
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: First directors and board of directors
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Hold the first board meeting or pass a unanimous written resolution. Adopt the pro-forma First Board Resolution contained in this dossier, recording adoption of the MOI, acceptance of share subscriptions, appointment of officers, registered office address, financial year-end, banking authorities and appointment of an auditor or independent reviewer if required. Minutes must be signed and maintained in the statutory records of the company.
required_dossiers: Consent to Act forms for appointed officers
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Disputes concerning share subscription or director appointments are resolved in accordance with the MOI and s66 of the Companies Act. Correct the minutes, re-execute consents, and file any subsequent changes with CIPC using the appropriate CoR forms.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Mandatory Post-Incorporation Tax and Employment Registrations
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: South African Revenue Service (SARS) via eFiling; Department of Employment and Labour (for COIDA/UIF)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After receiving the CIPC registration certificate, verify automatic income tax registration through SARS eFiling. Register for VAT if taxable supplies exceed or are expected to exceed R1 million per annum. If employees are engaged, register as an employer for Pay-As-You-Earn (PAYE), Unemployment Insurance Fund (UIF) and Workmen's Compensation / COIDA. Complete all registrations before commencing trading or hiring staff.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If SARS returns a non-compliance notice, promptly supply outstanding documents and correct business data. Late registration penalties may be challenged through the SARS dispute or waiver procedure with a covering explanation and evidence of good cause.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable — EdTech subscription and automated tutoring software do not constitute industrial or manufacturing operations and therefore do not require a permit from an industrial licensing board.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: No sectoral operating licence is required for online language-education services. A standard municipal business registration may be required if a physical office is opened.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Department of Forestry, Fisheries and the Environment (DFFE)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt — no listed activity under the EIA Regulations, 2014 Listing Notices is triggered by a purely digital service platform; no construction, land alteration or effluent-generating infrastructure is involved.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not applicable at the point of registration. If a physical office is later established, electronic waste disposal must comply with the National Environmental Management: Waste Act (Act 59 of 2008), and general waste handling must meet municipal by-laws and SANS 10400 requirements.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Not required for a purely virtual EdTech operation. If a commercial office is occupied, the lessor must supply a Certificate of Occupancy confirming compliance with the National Building Regulations, and the local fire authority must issue a fire safety clearance before staff physically begin work.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: South African Revenue Service (SARS); eFiling portal at https://www.sarsefiling.co.za
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Register the foreign entity as an external company with the Companies and Intellectual Property Commission (CIPC) under the Companies Act 71 of 2008. Thereafter apply for income tax registration with SARS via eFiling by submitting the CIPC registration extract, constitutional documents, and SARS registration forms. Upon acceptance, SARS issues a 10-digit income tax reference number (TIN). If the person supplies taxable supplies that cross the VAT registration threshold, file a VAT101 application through eFiling or a SARS branch, whereupon a VAT vendor number is issued.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation — a South African resident company is taxed as a separate taxpayer on worldwide income; a foreign external company carrying on a South African trade is taxed on income with a South African source or deemed source, without pass-through attribution.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: South Africa does not operate a US-style check-the-box entity classification election; entity treatment follows legal form and tax residence. Relevant elections are (i) the headquarter-company election under section 9I of the Income Tax Act 58 of 1962 for qualifying South African resident companies with at least 80% foreign ownership; (ii) the VAT group election under section 50 of the Value-Added Tax Act 89 of 1991, allowing group members to be treated as a single vendor; and (iii) hybrid financial instrument and hybrid entity rules apply mandatorily under sections 8F, 8E and related provisions, with no elective mismatch treatment.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value-Added Tax (VAT) under the Value-Added Tax Act 89 of 1991, administered by SARS
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: ZAR 1,000,000 (compulsory VAT registration when taxable supplies exceed or are likely to exceed ZAR 1 million in any 12 consecutive months; a foreign supplier of electronic services, including EdTech subscription services, is obliged to register for South African VAT irrespective of the ZAR 1 million threshold)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: South Africa does not currently impose real-time fiscal clearance, API-driven pre-clearance, or digital stamping for VAT invoices. SARS accepts electronic tax invoices provided they satisfy the form and content requirements of section 20 of the VAT Act. SARS eFiling and SARS eInvoicing facilitate electronic filing and document exchange, but issuance and retention remain on an audit-basis rather than a transactional clearance mandate.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Goods are zero-rated where they are genuinely exported from South Africa, evidenced by the Customs export declaration and proof of export within 60 days of the tax invoice date unless an extended period has been granted by SARS. Services are zero-rated under section 11(2)(l) of the VAT Act where the recipient is a non-resident who is outside South Africa at the time of supply and the services are not directly connected with South African immovable or movable property. Digital language-learning subscription services supplied to foreign non-resident end users qualify as exported services where the use and benefit of the service occurs outside South Africa.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Bill of Lading / Airway Bill evidencing actual exportation
Inward Foreign Remittance Certificate or bank payment statement evidencing receipt of export consideration
Copy of the VAT invoice and contract with the foreign customer
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: SARS will disallow zero-rating and claw back 15% VAT, plus interest, where the requisite export documentation is missing or the vendor fails to prove that services were supplied to a non-resident for offshore consumption. The Tax Administration Act 28 of 2011 imposes understatement penalties determined by conduct, reaching 150% of the assessed shortfall for intentional tax evasion. Fraudulent zero-rating claims, false customs declarations, and false invoices may trigger criminal prosecution under the Customs and Excise Act and the Tax Administration Act, with imprisonment exposure. For exchange control purposes, failure to remit export proceeds within 180 days may also expose the company to administrative penalties imposed by the Financial Surveillance Department of the South African Reserve Bank.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: South African Reserve Bank (SARB), acting through its Financial Surveillance Department (FinSurv), which administers the Exchange Control Regulations promulgated under the Currency and Exchanges Act 9 of 1933 (as amended), in conjunction with Authorised Dealers (South African banking institutions licensed as foreign exchange dealers) and Authorised Dealers in Foreign Exchange with Limited Authority.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: South Africa operates a dual-regime convertibility framework. Current-account flows (EdTech subscription export revenue, intercompany service fees, royalties, and profit/dividend remittances) are freely convertible: ZAR may be sold to an Authorised Dealer for such payments upon production of supporting commercial documentation, without requiring prior SARB approval. Capital-account flows (foreign equity subscription, intercompany loans, offshore treasury placements and acquisitions) remain subject to residual exchange-control approvals under the Currency and Exchanges Act; Authorised Dealers may approve standard inward and outward transactions within delegated limits, while amounts above thresholds (for example, inward loans in aggregate exceeding approximately ZAR 15 million) or structurally complex arrangements require express FinSurv approval. Profit remittance hurdles are documentary rather than substantive: remitting dividends to non-resident shareholders requires (i) Form MP336 (annual dividend application), (ii) audited financial statements or an auditor's confirmation of distributable reserves satisfying the Companies Act (No. 71 of 2008) s.46 solvency and liquidity test, (iii) a SARS tax status certificate and proof of 20% dividends tax withheld or exempted, and (iv) beneficiary identity consistent with CRS/FATCA records. Interest and principal repayment on inward loans requires registration of the inward loan with the Authorised Dealer/FinSurv (purpose code 100090) and compliance with the minimum tenor and arm's-length interest provisions of the prevailing FinSurv loan guidelines. No convertibility restriction applies to bona fide current-account receipts, provided the underlying documentation demonstrates genuine trade in services.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Under Exchange Control Regulation 8 and the FinSurv Exchange Control Manual, every exporter of goods or services - including cross-border digital education services and app-store subscription revenue - must take all reasonable steps to ensure that the full value of export proceeds is received in South Africa through an Authorised Dealer within the prescribed period (currently 90 days from date of invoice or settlement for service exports, as extended by FinSurv updates; a 180-day extension may be applied for on demonstrable commercial grounds). Proceeds must be repatriated into the exporter's domestic ZAR account or a Foreign Currency Account (FCA) maintained with an Authorised Dealer; repatriation itself is compulsory. Since the 2016-2017 exchange-control liberalisation, there is no mandatory conversion ratio: the historical requirement to surrender a fixed percentage of export receipts to ZAR has been abolished, and exporters may retain 100% of proceeds in an FCA and convert at their discretion on prevailing commercial rates. A formal surrender certificate is not required for service exports, but proceeds must be identifiably trade-related and traceable to the underlying export contracts. For EdTech revenue settled through Apple App Store or Google Play Billing, the South African contracting entity (ZA_PTY_LTD) must ensure that marketplace net remittances are routed to its South African bank account within the 90-day receipt window; platform commissions of 15-30% must be substantiated by periodic platform settlement reports, and any retention of proceeds offshore beyond the permitted period, or conversion undertaken outside an Authorised Dealer, constitutes an exchange-control offence attracting penalties and potential enforcement action.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Standard Bank of South Africa Limited
FirstRand Bank Limited (trading as First National Bank / FNB)

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Offshore digital EMI platforms (Wise Business, Airwallex, Payoneer, Currencycloud and similar) are not licensed by SARB as banks or Authorised Dealers and cannot lawfully serve as the primary settlement venue for South African export receipts: channelling EdTech subscription proceeds to a foreign EMI account would breach the export-proceeds receipt and repatriation rules of Exchange Control Regulation 8, unless the foreign account is an approved Foreign Currency Account established through a South African Authorised Dealer. Feasibility rating: LOW as a ZAR corporate treasury hub and as a primary collection rail for ZA_PTY_LTD; MEDIUM as an auxiliary international disbursement rail (payments to overseas contractors, content licences and marketing agencies), provided all funds are moved onward via SWIFT MT103 into the South African operational account, each transaction is supported by underlying commercial agreements, and transfer-pricing documentation is retained. Wise and similar providers operate in South Africa only through licensed partner bank clearing infrastructure; a standalone EMI venue fronting ZAR for a South African entity is legally unavailable.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Under the Financial Intelligence Centre Act 38 of 2001 (FICA), s.21, read with the FIC Guidance Note 6, physical appearance of directors is not a statutory mandate for a low-risk standard corporate client; the tier-1 banks permit remote onboarding through dual-verification e-KYC (liveness-checked video interview, near-field-communication passport scan and independent biometric acceptance) where the corporate risk profile is standard and the beneficial ownership chain is transparent. Remote opening is generally available for a company whose directors are non-resident, subject to enhanced due diligence: sanctions screening, PEP screening, adverse-media checks and tax-residency verification of each director and beneficial owner. Practical friction points: where any shareholder or signatory is tax-resident in a high-risk or blacklisted jurisdiction, the bank will effectively require a physical branch interview of at least one in-country authorised signatory or a South African-resident director; otherwise a combined video-plus-branch-hub verification is accepted. Recommended mandate for ZA_PTY_LTD: appoint one South African-resident authorised signatory (or use the bank's dedicated corporate KYC team with a video interview) to achieve a 2-3 week onboarding timeline; present the complete FICA client information profile, beneficial-ownership schedule in the prescribed Reg 17A form, and board resolution approving account opening.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident beneficial owners (foreign shareholders of ZA_PTY_LTD) presenting no verifiable South African economic or tax nexus at account-opening screening.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Corporate identification pack: (i) certified passport pages or e-verification output for each director and every shareholder holding 25% or more; (ii) utility statements or bank statements (3 months) proving residential address for each individual; (iii) beneficial-ownership schedule in the FICA Reg 17A prescribed format and Companies Act s.50 register extract; (iv) certificate of incorporation, memorandum of incorporation and share register; (v) SARS income-tax registration confirmation (company profile); (vi) CRS/FATCA tax-residency self-certifications and registry extracts for each foreign entity/individual in the ownership chain; (vii) board resolution sealing applicant authority and signatory mandate; (viii) group organogram evidencing the full chain to ultimate beneficial owners.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Inbound foreign subscription capital flagged as unexplained third-party funds or rapid round-trip funding patterns inconsistent with the entity's EdTech operating profile.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Source-of-funds and source-of-wealth bundle: (i) 12 months of original bank statements of each remitting shareholder (English or sworn translation); (ii) executed share subscription agreement, board allotment resolution and allotment register under Companies Act s.38-40; (iii) Form MP336A currency declaration for inward share issues and the Authorised Dealer's inward-remittance confirmation; (iv) independent accountant's affirmation of the capital receipt and its application; (v) tax clearance certificates of the shareholders where relevant; (vi) share certificates and CIPC filings after allotment; (vii) a written narrative (supported by legal-pad confirmation where requested by the Financial Crime Compliance team) explaining the origin of funds, including sale of prior business, accumulated salary, dividends or realised investments.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-volume, low-value recurring credits from Apple App Store and Google Play Billing aggregates, potentially interpreted as co-mingled third-party flows, unlicensed money-service activity or marketplace pass-through.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: (i) Executed Apple Developer Program Agreement and Google Play Commerce Agreement evidencing the marketplace agency structure and 15-30% commission deduction; (ii) 12-month settlement reports from Apple and Google identifying net payouts, currency pairs and bank routing; (iii) a treasury reconciliation pack matching each settlement batch to user subscription transactions by country, store and date; (iv) zero-rating memorandum confirming the digital service export treatment for VAT purposes; (v) SOC 2 Type II attestation or ISO/IEC 27001 certificate of the EdTech platform's billing sub-processors; (vi) sample customer purchase receipts evidencing consumption-based sales and no unrelated-party pass-through; (vii) an independent auditor's letter confirming that the inflows constitute own-account service revenue of ZA_PTY_LTD.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions or PEP engine hits caused by user geolocation data, app-store sales in sanctioned territories or beneficial-owner name collisions (false positives generated by the bank's name-screening and transaction-monitoring systems).
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: (i) Platform geo-restriction statements from Apple and Google confirming prohibition of sales in OFAC-, EU- or UN-sanctioned territories; (ii) the bank's own sanctions-screening output with documented false-positive analysis; (iii) passport or government-issued identification for the matched individual and a legal opinion assessing name variation; (iv) transaction-lineage report identifying each screened transaction and its commercial context; (v) a written submission to the bank's Financial Crime Compliance team under the risk-based approach of FICA; (vi) where relevant, a SARB/FinSurv liaison letter confirming no exchange-control breach; (vii) an export-control assessment affirming no dual-use or ITAR/export-administration restriction applicable to the EdTech content.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant routing for foreign subscription capital into ZA_PTY_LTD: (1) select an Authorised Dealer bank maintaining both the Capital Escrow Account (for share capital and shareholder loans) and the Operational ZAR Account (for marketplace receipts and disbursements); (2) execute the share subscription or loan agreement, board resolution and, for loan structures, the SARB inward-loan application where aggregate principal equals or exceeds approximately ZAR 15 million, including documentary evidence of minimum tenor (currently no less than two years under the FinSurv loan guidelines) and arm's-length interest; (3) initiate the inward wire via SWIFT MT103 from the shareholder's own account (no cryptocurrency-backed remittance, no cash couriers, no third-party aggregators) quoting SARB purpose code 100120 for foreign equity investment or 100090 for foreign loans; (4) ensure the Authorised Dealer logs the receipt under the International Transactions Recording System and, for equity, records the allotment in the company's share register and files the necessary CIPC reconciliation; (5) convert proceeds at an arm's-length spot rate or retain the balance in an approved Foreign Currency Account at the corporate's discretion; (6) for operational receipts from Apple App Store and Google Play Billing, direct the payment platforms' treasury payout protocols to remit net settlement into the Operational Account, retaining Apple/Google settlement dashboards, payout receipts and reconciliation reports; (7) retain all underlying agreements, bank SWIFT confirmations, FX contracts, SARS declarations and FinSurv correspondence for at least five years in line with FICA record-keeping obligations.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Clearing rails for outbound treasury and trade settlements: (i) service and royalty payments (overseas software licensing, AI sub-processors, cloud hosting, content licences) via SWIFT MT103 customer credit transfers quoting SARB purpose code 41100 (royalties/licensing) or 42100 (professional/business services), supported by the underlying agreement, invoice, transfer-pricing documentation under s.31 of the Income Tax Act 58 of 1962 and, where relevant, withholding tax certificates or SARS exemption certificates; (ii) trade settlement for imported hardware, infrastructure or content via commercial letters of credit issued under UCP600 (SWIFT MT700 issuance, MT707 amendment, MT756 payment advice), generally through the same Authorised Dealer and documented with the export-import set-off dispensation where applicable; (iii) dividend distributions to non-resident shareholders via MT103 accompanied by Form MP336, audited distributable-reserves confirmation and proof of 20% dividends tax (or exemption under a double-taxation agreement); (iv) repayment of foreign shareholder loans strictly against the registered inward-loan record and agreed amortisation schedule; (v) intercompany recharges on an arm's-length basis with an OECD-aligned transfer-pricing policy to prevent recharacterisation as dividends; (vi) all outbound payments subject to the Authorised Dealer's fiduciary oversight under the Exchange Control Regulations, with transaction-level documentation retained for audit by FinSurv or SARS.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable Forwards (DF) in USD/ZAR, EUR/ZAR and GBP/ZAR executed onshore with an Authorised Dealer, maturities up to 12 months, covering identified commercial (current-account) exposures, with rollover permitted only on a fully covered and documented basis.

Foreign Currency Accounts (FCA) holding export receipts and app-store settlement proceeds as a natural liquidity buffer and balance-sheet hedge against ZAR depreciation, with conversion timing at the corporate's discretion subject to the 90-day repatriation receipt rule.

Cross-Currency Swaps (CCS) and Cross-Currency Interest Rate Swaps permitted for hedging permitted capital-account exposures (foreign-currency loans, equity-funded capital expenditure) where the underlying exposure is documented and, for complex structures or amounts above Authorised Dealer delegated limits, prior FinSurv authorisation is obtained.

FX Options and zero-cost collars (participating forwards, fences and collars) offered by Authorised Dealers for risk-management purposes only, with option premiums and settlements recorded as treasury expenses and evidenced by ISDA-style master documentation or bank-standard option confirmations.

NDFs (Non-Deliverable Forwards) are not permissible for onshore resident corporates because the ZAR is fully deliverable through the onshore interbank market; accessing offshore NDF markets would require specific FinSurv approval, and therefore NDFs are excluded from the standard permissible hedging mandate of ZA_PTY_LTD.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: CIPC Annual Return (turnover tier R1m–R10m) including beneficial ownership confirmation declaration
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 30 business days after the anniversary date of the company's incorporation each year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: CIPC late filing penalty per published tariff, compliance notice, suspension of active status, and involuntary deregistration if annual returns remain unfiled for two or more consecutive years (s82 Companies Act 71/2008).

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual financial statements delivered to shareholders
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Shareholders and board of directors; not filed with CIPC for private companies
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 6 months after the financial year-end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Directors may be personally liable for non-compliance; court could impose a delinquency declaration and administrative penalties.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Beneficial ownership register update after any shareholding transfer
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 30 days after any change in beneficial ownership or share transfer event
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file is an offence under the Companies Act; CIPC may impose administrative penalties and the company's registration status may be suspended.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Audit mandatory if Public Interest Score is 350 or more; independent review required for PIS between 100 and 349; below 100 and owner-controlled companies may be exempt from both audit and independent review unless the MOI requires otherwise.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS or IFRS for SMEs as permitted under South African Companies Act and financial reporting regulations

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The CIPC annual return requires a declaration confirming that the company's beneficial ownership register is current and accurate; all share transfers during the year must be recorded in the register and the updated beneficial ownership filing lodged with CIPC within 30 days of the change.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: US$1,500 – US$6,000 for full audit; US$800 – US$2,500 for independent review

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 27% (South African normal tax for companies with years of assessment ending on or after 31 March 2023)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No statutory tax holidays. Preferential deductions include: s11D research and development enhancement, s12H learnership allowances, s12B renewable-energy and s12C capital allowances, and the Small Business Corporation graduated rate structure for qualifying companies. Assessed losses carry forward indefinitely but are ring-fenced by the 80% utilisation cap.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: ITR14 (Income Tax Return for Companies) submitted electronically through SARS eFiling
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within 12 months of the end of the company's year of assessment, unless a shorter date is stated in the SARS notice; a non-resident company with a South African permanent establishment uses the branch financial year-end.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Legal name, company registration number, income tax reference number, and SARS eFiling profile details.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident company must first register as a South African taxpayer if it has a local PE or taxable South African-source income; the resident shareholder's details are not entered on this return.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Dates of the tax period covered by the return.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter the South African branch's accounting period, which must match the year of assessment notified by SARS.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: All worldwide receipts and accruals of a resident company; for a non-resident, only South African-source gross income attributable to a PE or taxable source.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If no PE exists in South Africa, pure EdTech subscription income from South African users is generally not taxable in South Africa unless characterised as a royalty; do not file ITR14 for that income.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Local and foreign dividends qualifying for exemption, interest from certain regulated funds, and treaty-protected income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Treaty-protected business profits must be excluded only when supported by PE determinations and residence certification.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 5 - Allowable Deductions and Capital Allowances
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: s11(a) trading expenses, s11D R&D, s12B renewable energy, s12C machinery allowances, s12H learnership deductions, and provision for bad debts.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Deduct only expenditure actually incurred for the production of taxable South African income; head-office costs must satisfy transfer pricing and allocation rules.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Balance of prior-year assessed losses to be set off, subject to the 80% of taxable income limitation.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Branch losses are carried forward only against future South African PE income, limited to the PE's taxable income and subject to continuity-of-trade tests.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 7 - Taxable Income and Normal Tax
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Apply the 27% corporate rate; SBC graduated rates apply where the entity qualifies.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply the same return but include only PE taxable income; final amount is now payable or carried to provisional tax account.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing attracts an Administrative Non-Compliance Penalty (ANP) under s210 TAA (up to ZAR 10,000 per day for large businesses and ZAR 250 per day for other taxpayers, subject to annual caps). A deficient return triggers an understatement penalty from 10% to 200% depending on behaviour, plus prescribed-rate interest and daily surcharges on unpaid tax.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: IRP6 (Provisional Tax Return) filed via SARS eFiling
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: First provisional payment and return within six months after the first day of the year of assessment; second provisional payment and return no later than the last business day of the year of assessment; optional third top-up declaration and payment within six months after financial year-end.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: SARS income tax reference number and provisional tax assessment period.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Only a non-resident company with a South African PE is a provisional taxpayer; a fully non-resident company without a PE is not registrable for IRP6.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Reasonable estimate of the full year's taxable income, based on the previous year's basic amount and current trading results.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Estimate must cover only South African PE profits; intercompany recharges must be aligned with the approved transfer pricing method.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Calculated tax at 27% on estimated taxable income, after deducting primary rebates, foreign tax credits, and prior payments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Application of DTA foreign tax credits to PE income must be supported by valid foreign tax assessments.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Signed confirmation that the estimate is honest, complete, and defensible.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The representative director of the branch must confirm that transfer pricing and permanent establishment documentation are contemporaneous.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: If an estimate is materially below actual taxable income, SARS imposes a 20% additional tax in terms of s218 TAA on the difference between tax on the estimate and tax on 80% of actual taxable income; late payment bears prescribed-rate interest and ANP continues for every day of non-compliance.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 20% on the gross amount of a dividend paid by a South African resident company, applied by the company as withholding agent.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Before the dividend is paid, the non-resident beneficial owner must provide the paying company with a valid SARS-prescribed declaration and a foreign tax residence certificate (TRC) issued by its treaty residence authority. The company applies the DTA rate, retains the paperwork, and reports the payment on the DTR02 dividends tax return. Without a valid declaration, the 20% rate is withheld conclusively.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory royalty withholding tax is 15%; statutory interest withholding tax is 15%. Under applicable DTAs the rate is commonly reduced to between 0% and 10% for both royalties and interest, subject to the same declaration, TRC, and beneficial-ownership conditions.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: ZAR 5,000,000 aggregate annual connected-person cross-border transactions and interest-bearing arrangements triggers contemporaneous transfer pricing documentation; multinational groups with consolidated turnover of at least ZAR 10,000,000,000 must file a Country-by-Country report and should retain Master File and Local File documentation on request.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: South Africa does not administer a separate 'ESR' statute in the offshore sense, but the GAAR under s80A-80L disregards transactions that lack commercial substance, s31 recharacterises transfer pricing without real functional allocation, s9D attributes undistributed CFC profits, and the MLI Principal Purpose Test denies treaty benefits. An EdTech structure holding excessive profits or IP in a zero-tax jurisdiction with no employees, premises, or decision-making will fail these substance standards.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberate understatement of South African user subscription revenue, fabrication of expenses, destruction of accounting records, or submission of a false ITR14.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Criminal offence under the Tax Administration Act 28 of 2011; on conviction, imprisonment for up to five years and/or a fine. Civil understatement penalty of 200% for intentional tax evasion, plus prescribed-rate interest and collection costs.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who cause or participate in the evasion may be prosecuted, ordered to make restitution, and subjected to preservation and travel-banishment orders; the corporate veil can be pierced under the Companies Act 71 of 2008 if the company was used fraudulently.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Paying a connected offshore entity excessive royalties, platform development fees, or management fees to erode South African profit, with no valid benchmark or contemporaneous transfer pricing file.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: SARS adjusts the consideration to an arm's length price under s31, disallows the excessive deduction, imposes an understatement penalty of up to 200%, and levies interest from the original due date.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who sign or approve the return may be personally assessed for unpaid withholding or corporate tax if the arrangement is a reportable arrangement designed to avoid tax, and the company's assets are dissipated.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Use of a letterbox Pty Ltd with no office, staff, or decision-making; formal ownership of EdTech IP in a zero-tax jurisdiction; or treaty shopping through a shell holding company.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: GAAR permits SARS to combine, disregard, or re-characterise the transaction; the MLI Principal Purpose Test denies treaty protection; the CFC provisions of s9D attribute the underlying profit to South African shareholders; an understatement penalty of 100%-200% may apply.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who implement a structure with a sole or main purpose of tax avoidance may be jointly and severally liable for evaded tax, exposed to civil damages, disqualified under the Companies Act, and barred from leaving South Africa under restraint orders.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Dividends / Interest / Royalty Withholding Tax Default
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Paying dividends to non-resident shareholders without applying the 20% dividends tax, paying royalties or interest offshore without 15% withholding, or applying treaty rates without the required declaration and TRC.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Withholding tax becomes a statutory debt due by the company as agent; SARS recovers the unpaid amount together with a 10%-200% understatement penalty and daily prescribed-rate interest, on top of the original tax.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be held personally liable for withholding taxes under the Tax Administration Act when the company disposes of assets, fails to pay the liability, and is placed in liquidation; travel bans and director disqualification are available remedies.
